newsitem.title: UK: City of Moscow plans $100 mln financing facility.
newsitem.headline: City of Moscow plans $100 mln financing facility.

text.p: LONDON, July 31 (LPC) - The City of Moscow is returning to the syndicated loan market with a $100 million syndicated trade financing facility, which is being arranged by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

Banking sources have been surprised by the City's swift reappearance only one month after its successful $200 million debut syndicated loan was concluded and are attributing the unusually fast followup to the City's attempt to capitalise on the momentum of the first deal.

The new credit is in the name of the City of Moscow's Department of City Development and the one-year facility, which is priced at 325 bps over LIBOR, will be used to finance the construction of residential buildings in Moscow. The credit has a 30-day availability period, and banks are being asked for minimum commitments of $1 million.

The deal has an unusual structure, lenders will not receive the customary fees for their participation, but will instead be given International Depository Receipts on settlement. The structure is said to have been adopted as less documentation is required, which has led banks to speculate that the City needed to raise funds quickly.

The City of Moscow's successful debut credit, arranged by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Societe Generale and West Merchant Bank, was originally launched as a $50 million transaction, but market appetite for the name meant that the deal was increased twice to $200 million.

While the new deal undercuts the margin of the City's previous deal by 25 bps, pricing still appears generous in comparison with the recently mandated credit for Sberbank, Russia's largest bank, which is priced at 200 bps. For further details go to LOANS
